scenarios.name: The booted server answers its liveness probe
scenarios.description: The cheapest real assertion in the suite, and the one that tells a failing run whether the target URL was even right. GET /api/v1/health is the unauthenticated liveness probe (packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts), so this scenario passes with or without --token — a failure here means the --url is wrong or the server is down, not that the data assertions below are broken.

scenarios.name: A record created through the data API reads back by the id the create returned
scenarios.description: The load-bearing scenario: it can only pass if capture, {{variable}} interpolation and assertion evaluation all work, because the read step's URL is built from the id the create step captured. showcase_category is the target because it is sharingModel: public_read_write with exactly one required field (examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/category.object.ts), so the record is legal on stock fixtures. Requires --token (a signed-in session); the data routes enforce auth.

steps.name: create a category
steps.description: POST /api/v1/data/:object — the wire body IS the record (#3899).

steps.name: read it back by the captured id
steps.description: The target carries {{categoryId}}: if capture or interpolation is dead, this GET asks for the literal path segment and the step fails instead of silently passing.

steps.name: find it in the list response
steps.description: `contains` over an array — the operator whose non-evaluable shapes used to pass silently (#7256). The field path points at a real array so the assertion is evaluated, not skipped.

teardown.name: delete the category
teardown.description: Teardown runs even after a failed step, so a red run does not leave the fixture dirty for the next one.
